lessons.title: Practice Top-K Retrieval
lessons.description: Implement topk(query, corpus, k) returning indices of k highest dots, highest first. The test checks that topk([1, 0], [[1, 0], [0, 1], [2, 0]], 2) equals [2, 0].
learning_objectives: This step reads the second highest score, using scores and 2.
lessons.solution_code:
def topk(query, corpus, k):
    scored = [(sum(a * b for a, b in zip(query, v)), i) for i, v in enumerate(corpus)]
    scored.sort(key=lambda t: (-t[0], t[1]))
    return [i for _, i in scored[:k]]

source.name: Dive into Deep Learning §2.3 — dot products ranked across vectors

lessons.title: Practice Mean Pool Tokens
lessons.description: Implement mean_pool(token_vecs) averaging equal-length vectors. The test checks that mean_pool([[1, 2], [3, 4]]) equals [2.0, 3.0].
learning_objectives: This step averages the first column of the vectors, using vecs and 1.
lessons.solution_code:
def mean_pool(token_vecs):
    dim = len(token_vecs[0])
    n = len(token_vecs)
    return [sum(v[d] for v in token_vecs) / n for d in range(dim)]

source.name: Dive into Deep Learning §2.3 — averaging vectors element-wise

lessons.title: Practice Checkpoint Softmax Scores
lessons.description: Implement softmax(xs) for a list of floats. The test checks that softmax([0, 0])[0] equals 0.5; sum(softmax([1, 2, 3])) equals 1.0.
learning_objectives: This step reads the larger softmax share, using xs and 2.
lessons.starter_code:
import math

def softmax(xs):
    # TODO
    pass
lessons.solution_code:
import math

def softmax(xs):
    m = max(xs)
    exps = [math.exp(x - m) for x in xs]
    s = sum(exps)
    return [e / s for e in exps]

tests.name: test_softmax
tests.unittest_code:
def test_softmax(self):
    out = softmax([0, 0])
    self.assertAlmostEqual(out[0], 0.5)
    self.assertAlmostEqual(sum(softmax([1, 2, 3])), 1.0)
